A FEW WAYS IN

Follow your curiosity.

Drag the canvas to move the finish point in the current view; the view stays fixed during the drag and fits the curves afterward. The distance/drop sliders give exact endpoints. Left/right changes horizontal reach; up/down changes vertical drop. Space or R replays the race. Gravity changes all travel times by the same inverse-square-root factor. Playback speed slows or accelerates the animation without restarting it. P pauses; geometry, replay and PNG export still work while paused. Reduced motion starts paused with all three tracks visible. Tracks: 1 cycloid, 2 straight, 3 parabola.

The mathematics

Three frictionless point masses start from rest at the same point and descend under uniform gravity: 1 cyan cycloid, 2 warm straight line, and 3 violet parabola. The cycloid is the minimum-time curve for these endpoints; it may dip below the finish and climb back. Its parameter and the straight-line motion have exact time laws. The parabola y = Y(2u−u²), x = Xu uses energy v² = 2gy and a bounded travel-time table with Simpson quadrature. A squared parameter removes the starting integrable singularity. Balls slide rather than roll; their radius is illustrative. The timing bars show total travel times, with moving progress markers. Balls stop at the finish without a rebound. Changing geometry or gravity restarts the race; playback speed preserves its physics.
